_comment: TEMPLATE identity for a fresh Core. Edit every value below before first use. This file is per_core_keep, so sync NEVER overwrites it and whatever you put here stays yours. It previously shipped as a real person's live finance Core — their name, email, home directory and brokerage allowlist — and it carried no hook_profile.role, which made reconcile-hooks.py exit 2. The sync path swallowed that error, so a fresh Core installed 12 of 37 hooks and had no self-improvement spine at all, with nothing reported. Both problems are fixed here. Keep this file generic if you ever push it upstream.
_comment_org_id: Tenant id for this Core in the corebrain Postgres. A standalone Core keeps 1. Only assign 2, 3, 4 ... if you run SIBLING Cores against the SAME database — the ids must be unique per Core or their memory and learned rules collide.

hook_profile._comment: REQUIRED — must be exactly 'puller' or 'writer'. 'puller' syncs shared code FROM the baseline and never pushes back; that is correct for every Core except the single baseline writer. 'writer' is the one Core allowed to push shared code upstream. reconcile-hooks.py exits 2 on any other value, and that failure is silent, so a wrong value here costs you most of your hooks with no visible error.

_comment_sister_projects: Optional sibling Cores on this machine, e.g. [{"label": "work", "path": "/Users/you/Cores/work-core"}]. Leave empty for a single Core.
_comment_webfetch: Domains Core may fetch WITHOUT a Sentinel review. Keep this list tight and add your own tools deliberately — anything here bypasses the gate.
